architectureDecisions: H adds no RecoveryManager: each failure is recovered by the production owner of the affected claim, attempt, semantic-currentness, deployment/QA or product-history subject.
Failure injection uses deterministic barriers at durable boundaries; it cannot replace production CAS/currentness guards or add stronger serialization.
Execution recovery preserves semantic executionAttemptId + immutable binding; runtime invocation may change, but same-attempt recover/repair cannot re-resolve HOW or mint a new attempt.
Claim takeover is fenced by current claimGeneration/release; stale workers fail before dispatch/publication.
Committed DomainPublicationReceipt is continuation truth; restart derives downstream effects idempotently instead of rerunning accepted domain work.
Semantic-input drift uses delivered currentness + selective reverse invalidation; unrelated state is not widened into recovery scope.
Deployment/QA and closure recovery revalidate their exact release/projection heads; old evidence remains immutable history, not current acceptance.
Duplicate recovery converges through existing CAS heads and stable materialization/publication keys; any need for central sequencing/global reset is an architecture failure.
implementationSlices: H1 — Failure harness [AC-1..AC-10, INV-8]: deterministic test-only kill/pause barriers around production durable writes/guards; no sleeps or test-only stronger locks.
H2 — Claim/attempt recovery [AC-1, AC-3, AC-7, AC-8]: prove same-binding fresh-process recovery, stale-generation fencing, duplicate convergence and no repair-minted semantic attempt.

H3 — Publication/input-currentness recovery [AC-2, AC-4, AC-7, AC-10]: kill after publication and race semantic-input drift; reuse committed publication, converge one downstream continuation and invalidate only reverse dependents.
H4 — QA/closure races [AC-5, AC-6]: race DeploymentRelease with QA and upstream supersession with closure; preserve historical evidence while blocking stale current acceptance/outcome.
H5 — Product-history divergence [AC-9]: kill between closure-relevant authority movement and ProductHistory append; expose NOT_READY until deterministic fresh-process reconciliation.
H6 — End-to-end matrix [AC-1..AC-10]: reconstruct from durable stores, run all failures + B–G regressions, and require unaffected work to continue without global reset/manual order.
